key_insight: Low-Reynolds-number propeller thrust can exhibit transient hysteresis even when rotor-disk inflow, blade deformation, and sectional circulation remain largely quasi-steady.
engineering_relevance: Thrust models for small UAV speed control may need pitch-dependent transient corrections rather than relying solely on steady-state maps or dynamic inflow theory.
method: Tested a commercial two-bladed propeller in hover at pitch offsets of 0°, 5°, and 10°.
Applied open-loop acceleration and deceleration steps between 3000 and 5000 RPM.
Combined load measurements with phase-locked PIV at three radial stations and in the meridian plane.
evidence_signal: At the 5° pitch offset, thrust coefficients deviated from steady values by up to 8% during acceleration and 5% during deceleration, while wake-flow deviations were largest at low rotational speeds.
watch_item: The abstract gives conflicting descriptions of the 10° thrust response; verify the full paper before drawing pitch-specific conclusions.
paper_title: On the aerodynamics of an accelerating and decelerating propeller in hover at low Reynolds numbers
